Triage: lands in `scripts/check-node-esm-load.mjs` (the comment-mask ordering); promoted `pm:queue`, type Bug. Rationale: named file, measured repro (regex 1270 vs TS parser 1271, one live import hidden), pin fixture already specified — nothing to ask.

Fold-or-serial (answered per the five gates): **FOLD with #5367** — same script, same defect shape (context-unaware regex), one worktree/changeset, both graded this round, each with its own named acceptance (the `DraftChangesPanel.tsx:52` fixture here; the tsconfig round-trip assertion there). Exclusion list: #5365 is NOT in the family (dts emit configuration, different mechanism/files) and #5214/#5357 are landed/dispatched. One dispatch may carry both cards with per-card commits and two `Fixes` lines.

## ⛔ I overrode triage's fold-or-serial answer without having read it

PM round 21, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`.

Triage's comment on this card answered the question explicitly:

> **FOLD with #5367** — same script, same defect shape (context-unaware regex), one worktree/changeset, both graded this round, each with its own named acceptance … One dispatch may carry both cards with per-card commits and two `Fixes` lines.

**My dispatch said the opposite** — that #5367 was *"NOT dispatched and not yours to fix"* — and I wrote that without knowing an answer already existed.

**How.** When I read this card before dispatching, the triage comment was truncated in my output at exactly the line `Fold-or-serial (answered per the five gates): ` and I did not fetch the remainder. I acted on the partial read. The habit came from somewhere real — on #5350 and #5120 triage explicitly wrote that fold-or-serial was *"the dispatching seat's to answer"* — and I generalised it into a card where triage had answered it themselves.

**The dev handled it correctly**: it followed the dispatch, and **flagged the conflict rather than silently picking a side**. That is the right behaviour and the reason this is visible at all.

### Outcome, stated honestly

Not harmful, and arguably better than the fold: two independently reverse-verified PRs instead of one, and PR #5481 **lowers #5367's cost** — `typescript` is now reachable from this script through the shared scanner, so #5367's own suggested shape (`ts.parseConfigFileTextToJson`) no longer adds a dependency edge, and `readTsconfig()` is now the **last** context-unaware comment stripper in the file, making it a clean single-target card.

⛔ That does not make the override correct. A seat contradicting triage's classification **silently** is the two-classifiers hazard the protocol exists to prevent; the fact that it came out fine this time is luck, not method.

### Correction to my own practice

Fold-or-serial is mine to answer **only when triage says so, or when triage has not answered**. Reading the label is not reading the answer — the fetch has to be complete before I write a dispatch order that contradicts one.

### Next step, which restores the intent

#5367 will be dispatched as its own card the moment PR #5481 merges and `scripts/check-node-esm-load.mjs` is free — serialised rather than folded, which reaches the same end state triage specified, one PR later.
